data.name: Ghanshayam
data.gender_notes: Ghanshayam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ghanshayam is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Ghana' meaning 'Lord of the Universe' and 'Shayam' meaning 'Abode of Vishnu'. This name signifies the divine presence of Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. The name Ghanshayam carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ghanshayam usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ghanshayam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghanshayam total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ghanshayam' is deeply rooted in Hindu culture and is often used as a reverential name for Lord Vishnu, particularly in northern and western parts of India. It reflects the deep devotion and reverence that Hindus hold for their deities and the belief in the omnipresence of the divine. This name also holds significant importance in various Hindu scriptures and spiritual texts.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ghanshayam is considered a sacred name for the Lord and invoking it is believed to bring peace, happiness, prosperity, and divine blessings. It is a reminder of the presence of Vishnu, the eternal protector and nurturer, in everyday life. Chanting or reciting this name is believed to help purify the mind, deepen devotion, and amplify the spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ghanshayam: The name Ghanshayam signifies the one who carries the burden of the entire universe (Ghan) on a lotus (Shayam), symbolizing detachment and selflessness.
